terra.problem: “No shelf, no statue in the corner” rules out physical idols, which the passage does not do. It also does not say the idols were what the elders held closest.
The explanation identifies Ezekiel as a priest living among the exiles, facts outside this passage, without a reference.
The claim that idols appeared in high places elsewhere in the Bible needs a reference.
The question is not the first thing the LORD says about the elders. He first describes their idols and stumbling blocks.
The claim that Ezekiel and the people around him were living among the exiles is outside this passage and needs a reference.
The car comparison does not click: needing to turn around does not mean a person cannot enjoy the view until they do.
“He asks for a turning” softens the LORD's command to repent and turn away from idols into a request.
The passage says the elders came and sat before Ezekiel, not that they came to ask.
The claim about false prophets elsewhere in the Bible needs a reference.
The claim that God puts words in someone's mouth elsewhere in Scripture needs a reference.
“I understand the worry” assumes the baker is worried, which Papa Dorin has not been told.
